questions.q: What is SQL*Plus, per this lesson?
options: Oracle's original command-line client for running SQL and PL/SQL, well-suited to scripts and admin one-liners
A free graphical IDE for schema browsing and development
Oracle's enterprise-wide monitoring product
A tool used only to install the Oracle Database software
questions.explain: SQL*Plus is described as Oracle's original, script-friendly command-line interface — the closest thing to SQL Server's sqlcmd.

questions.q: What role does SQL Developer play, per this lesson?
options: Oracle's free, Java-based GUI IDE for browsing schema objects and writing/running SQL and PL/SQL, loosely comparable to SSMS
A command-line-only tool with no graphical interface
Oracle's primary backup and recovery utility
A monitoring dashboard for tracking database performance history
questions.explain: SQL Developer is Oracle's free GUI IDE, playing a role loosely similar to SQL Server Management Studio for schema browsing and SQL/PL-SQL development.

questions.q: What is the difference between EM Express and Enterprise Manager Cloud Control, per this lesson?
options: EM Express is a lightweight, web-based console bundled with the database for one database; Cloud Control is a separately-installed enterprise product for managing many databases
They are two names for the exact same product with no differences
EM Express manages many databases; Cloud Control only manages one
Cloud Control is bundled free with every database installation, while EM Express must be purchased separately
questions.explain: EM Express ships with the database for basic single-database monitoring, while Cloud Control is a full, separately-installed product for enterprise-wide management.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which tool is the best fit for writing a repeatable, scriptable admin task against an Oracle database?
options: SQL*Plus
SQL Developer
Enterprise Manager Cloud Control
EM Express
questions.explain: SQL*Plus is scriptable and doesn't depend on a GUI, making it the tool most admin scripts and one-liners are written for.

questions.q: What does Chapter 3 begin with, according to this lesson's outro?
options: Oracle authentication and user accounts
Oracle backup and recovery with RMAN
MySQL architecture and installation
Oracle performance tuning methodology
questions.explain: This lesson closes Chapter 2, and the outro teases Chapter 3's opening lesson on Oracle authentication and user accounts.
